frontmatter.title: The library supports saving Excel files as meta file EMF

blocks.content: Aspose.Cells enables Python developers to convert Excel workbooks to EMF (Enhanced Metafile) format, a vector graphics format suitable for high-quality rendering in Windows environments. This capability supports embedding scalable spreadsheet content—such as charts and tables—into documents, presentations, or other applications that consume EMF.

The library also supports saving Excel files to other formats like Markdown (MD), JSON, and more, offering flexibility for data exchange and documentation workflows. While the focus of this page is EMF conversion, the underlying `Workbook` class provides a unified interface for exporting diverse output types using the same core API.

from aspose_cells_foss import Workbook

# Instantiating a Workbook object
workbook = Workbook()
# Obtaining the reference of the newly added worksheet
sheet = workbook.worksheets[0]
cells = sheet.cells
cells.get("A1").put_value("First name")
cells.get("A2").put_value("Simon")
cells.get("B1").put_value("Age")
cells.get("B2").put_value(32)
# Saving the Excel file to EMF
workbook.save("output.emf")

The `Workbook` class serves as the primary in-memory representation of an Excel file in Aspose.Cells. Developers instantiate this class to create, load, or manipulate spreadsheets before saving them to various formats.

Data in Aspose.Cells is organized into `Worksheet` objects, each containing a grid of `Cell` objects accessible via `worksheets` and `cells` collections. Values are written using `put_value()` on individual cells.

The `save()` method on `Workbook` supports exporting to multiple formats, including EMF (Enhanced Metafile), Markdown (MD), and JSON. The output format is inferred from the file extension provided in the path argument.

from aspose_cells_foss import Workbook

workbook = Workbook()
sheet = workbook.worksheets[0]
cells = sheet.cells
cells.get("A1").put_value("First name")
cells.get("A2").put_value("Simon")
workbook.save("MarkDown.md")

Aspose.Cells enables conversion of Excel workbooks to EMF (Enhanced Metafile) format, a vector graphics format suitable for high-quality rendering in Windows environments. To save an Excel file as EMF, load the workbook and call the `save` method with a filename ending in .emf.

from aspose_cells_foss import Workbook

# Load an existing Excel file or create a new one
workbook = Workbook("Input.xlsx")
# Save the workbook as EMF
workbook.save("Output.emf")

Aspose.Cells supports exporting Excel data directly to Markdown (.md) format, making it easy to integrate spreadsheet content into documentation or web-based workflows. Specify a .md extension in the `save` method to trigger Markdown conversion.

from aspose_cells_foss import Workbook

# Instantiate a Workbook and populate data
workbook = Workbook()
sheet = workbook.worksheets[0]
cells = sheet.cells
cells.get("A1").put_value("Name")
cells.get("B1").put_value("Score")
cells.get("A2").put_value("Alice")
cells.get("B2").put_value(95)
# Save as Markdown
workbook.save("Report.md")

Aspose.Cells enables conversion of Excel workbooks to EMF (Enhanced Metafile) format, a vector graphics format suitable for high-quality rendering in Windows environments. The following example demonstrates loading a workbook, adding sample data and a column chart, then saving the result as an EMF file.

from aspose_cells_foss import Workbook
from aspose_cells_foss import ChartType

# Instantiating a Workbook object
workbook = Workbook()
# Adding a new worksheet to the Excel object
sheetIndex = workbook.worksheets.add()
# Obtaining the reference of the newly added worksheet by passing its sheet index
worksheet = workbook.worksheets[sheetIndex]
# Adding sample values to cells
worksheet.cells.get("A1").put_value(50)
worksheet.cells.get("A2").put_value(100)
worksheet.cells.get("A3").put_value(170)
worksheet.cells.get("A4").put_value(300)
worksheet.cells.get("B1").put_value(160)
worksheet.cells.get("B2").put_value(32)
worksheet.cells.get("B3").put_value(50)
worksheet.cells.get("B4").put_value(40)
# Adding sample values to cells as category data
worksheet.cells.get("C1").put_value("Q1")
worksheet.cells.get("C2").put_value("Q2")
worksheet.cells.get("C3").put_value("Y1")
worksheet.cells.get("C4").put_value("Y2")
# Adding a chart to the worksheet
chartIndex = worksheet.charts.add(ChartType.COLUMN, 5, 0, 15, 5)
# Accessing the instance of the newly added chart
chart = worksheet.charts[chartIndex]
# Adding SeriesCollection (chart data source) to the chart ranging from "A1" cell to "B4"
chart.n_series.add("A1:B4", True)
# Setting the data source for the category data of SeriesCollection
chart.n_series.category_data = "C1:C4"
# Saving the Excel file as EMF
workbook.save("Chart.emf")

Aspose.Cells enables conversion of Excel workbooks to multiple formats beyond standard spreadsheet types. In addition to EMF image output, the library supports exporting to Markdown, JSON, and other structured formats using the `Workbook.save()` method.
